text: Abandon leaking ship before the cruise - [Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly / Abandon leaking ship before the cruise Search for: Search forums Abandon leaking ship before the cruise chris4element (@chris4element) 2 years, 5 months ago First install of the bought Pro Version, I setup Google Calender Sync and Zoom Integration. This worked well. But then, first issue, I could double and triple book the same slot for one staff member. Bookly did recognise Google Calender entires, but not its own bookings. Second, booking user got added as wordpress users well, but not as Bookly user. It wasn’t even possible to add a customer manually from the backend! Unfortunately I ran out of support because I bought this license to long ago and did not use earlier. I thought of buying a second license for another site to get a new support possiblity. But then I investigated some more. The webiste itself is nothing fancy, newly set up, all sound. After I read many hints and experiences of things/problems like this, I decided to quit for good. I have become wise enough to choose my battles. And this is a uphill battle right from the start. Uninstallling and deleting took some time, the Bookly plugin does not clear the database. In fact, in addition to the main tables, there are an impressive number of entries scattered a bit all over the place. So be careful, bet on your luck, maybe I just caught a Monday morning version? The documentation is really excellent, but at least the most basic things have to work, don’t they? This topic was modified 2 years, 5 months ago by chris4element . Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support booklysupport (@booklysupport) 2 years, 5 months ago Hello, Here are some suggestions to address your concerns: Please review the staff and service capacity settings in Bookly. If the same time slot is already occupied by a customer and the staff or service capacity is set to a maximum of 1, Bookly won’t allow booking the slot again. If you’ve enabled the “Create WordPress user account for customers” setting in Bookly, new customer accounts will be generated. You can choose the role for these accounts under this setting. The available roles are determined by your WordPress configuration, and you can use third-party plugins to manage user roles on your website. In Bookly, under Settings > General > Bookly data upon deleting Bookly items, you can choose what happens to the associated data when you delete Bookly items (Bookly, Bookly Pro, or any Bookly add-ons). If you select “Delete”, all associated data will be permanently removed. If you encounter any issues or have further questions, please submit a support request here . Our team is dedicated to providing assistance and resolving any issues you may encounter. We strive to ensure that our product meets the highest standards of quality and customer satisfaction. Try to switch the “Method to include Bookly JavaScript and CSS files on the page” option to “Pages with Bookly form” (Bookly > Settings > General). Try to increase the WordPress memory limit. You can check what the memory limit is currently set in the WordPress > Tools > Site Health > Info > WordPress constants section. You can aggregate, minify and cache all scripts and styles of your website with any optimizing plugin. For example you can use https://wordpress.org/plugins/autoptimize/ . I’ve been using Bookly for several years on multiple sites. I have purchased many of the add-ons they require in order to make this a useful tool. It is probably the most unreliable plugin I have ever used. It requires constant attention to try to keep it working properly. I get calls and emails frequently from clients letting me know there are issues with their booking process. If you’re considering purchasing this plugin, beware, and be ready to spend a lot of cash on add-ons and service contracts once your 6 months expire. My most recent issue happened when WordPress updated to version 5.5. The Bookly dashboard stopped working and their customer service people wouldn’t do anything about it unless I paid their ransom for the service contract. I will not give these people another dime. I would highly recommend you try to find another solution to your booking requirements. Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 6 years, 1 month ago We’re sorry to hear that you ran into trouble. The latest update went smoothly for the absolute majority of users. Since Bookly is installed on your server, issues may occur because of other WP plugins, themes, and systems. Before every release, we thoroughly test our plugin to its highest quality, but we can’t guarantee that after update the plugin will work properly on all WordPress configurations and completely protect it from the influence of other plugins. There is a small risk that some issues may appear as a result of updating the plugin, and, unfortunately, according to Envato rules, we will be able to help you only if you have active support because technical assistance is a paid service available only during the active item support period. If you don’t want to renew your item support, we recommend not updating Bookly and stay on the version which works well for you. It is a pay trap. The only good thing about this plugin is their workflow like booking form, which is pretty well, made but thats about it. A ducking lot of other pretty basic stuff is hidden behind additional plugins as well. The pro version is not sufficient for most usages. Some of those basic features is mandatory in some countries so be sure to carefully go through their list of plugin-plugins to check what is missing. Unlike the claim in their advertisement the Pro version of this plugin is not fully customizable (except if you change the plugin file of course). There is a bunch of other plugins necessary to make it fully customizable. The most basic situations for a business/person offering time slots to “book” are not covered by the PRO version either. e.g. for exceptional working times you need to buy yet another plugin or change your default schedule temporarily, but since that one is specified in a weekly format you cannot offer bookings for those special days more than a week ahead. The pro version is not GDPR compliant . For that they offer yet another plugin. This topic was modified 6 years, 2 months ago by Jan Dembowski . No links or links to images. That’s not permitted in reviews and I have removed yours. I’ve also removed the tags from this review. That’s name calling and attacking anyone on this site has a short shelf life. You’ve used your words well and those tags are not needed and too far. Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 6 years, 2 months ago We understand that the out-of-the-box solution cannot fit for everyone all the time and sorry to hear that default Bookly PRO doesn’t correspond to your expectations. We regularly include new features in the default version, which makes it one of the most feature-rich booking solutions in the market. We believe that the prices for Bookly and its add-ons are reasonable enough because it’s a one-time purchase that is in itself a complex booking system. All prices are available in the portfolio, all products are available on multiple demos and materially similar to advertising materials. It seems like you think that the whole Bookly team should work for free. If you’re a programmer, you should be well aware of the development process. We advise you to create your own product and start distributing it for free to everyone. Once you do this – do not forget to let us know so we can also check the quality of your code and support. I give it two stars still because support is excellent when reaching out –*IF* you’re a paid customer of their pro version(s). I’ve given up on them though and will no longer recommend as they continue extricating features and selling them as add on’s to their already pricey enough pro version of the plugin. text: Service scheduling not smart enough - [Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly / Service scheduling not smart enough Search for: Search forums Service scheduling not smart enough nmxde (@nmxde) 4 years, 8 months ago Pro: beautiful design, flexible mail-templates Con: tracking integration (Google Analytics, Matomo) is a pain. Scheduling does not meet our buiness requirements: We offer services with different duration. Bookly is not smart enough to fill / prevent gaps. If someone picks a 9:15 slot, we’re sitting idle the first 15 minutes. If someome books a 15 minute service half a hour after the previous (and most of services take 45 minutes or more), then we’re idle for 30 minutes. This means a significant loss of revenue for us. The option to just show the next available slot without considering the customer’s availability doesn’t make sense because it would end the booking process for most customers (how likely is it that the customer is available at a specific random time?). Bookly product management doesn’t see any problem here… or doesn’t care too much about their (paid-) users need. Also, be careful with add-ons: some of them are absolutely useless (like the waiting list: you can “soft book” one specific timeslot that is already taken. How likely is it that just this one will become free?) This is related the pro-version, btw. I doubt that the free version can be use professionally due to its limitations. We believe that the default configuration fulfills the majority of our customers’ needs, and a comprehensive collection of paid plugins can meet any special requirements. This is in order not to overload the default version and each user chooses what features suit best for them and buy only those which are needed for their business. Please know that we value you as our customer and your concern is important to us. Search for: Search forums Fantastic Product, but support needs work. vicegodgiarc (@vicegodgiarc) 7 years ago Bookly “core” 17.6 is broken so rollback to 17.5 and working fine. Support is needs to be paid for. Yes so if you update breaks and your paid support has run out, dont expect a fix until you renew your “Support” Quote “Im afraid your item support for Bookly PRO – Appointment Booking and Scheduling Software System has ended on xxx. Could you please renew it, so I can go ahead and help you with your concern?” – go %^&* yourselves. The “core” was broken, not Pro. If you tested your code and releases this would not happen. Not the first time I have had issues. Read the other reviews for an understanding of “supprt” and “feature changes” They dont test code releases or update change documents very well. I hate upating this crap as the updates need a full end to end test to check functionality is still available. Yes its “great” software but comes with a heavy time consuming “price” BACKUP WEBSITE BEFORE UPDATES! This topic was modified 7 years ago by vicegodgiarc . Reason: Addon Updates were not available when 17.6 released Viewing 5 replies - 1 through 5 (of 5 total) TheSickle (@thesickle) 7 years ago Yesss thank you for this. I have been reporting and complaining about their Horrible support for months now. Exactly the same things they said to me as well. They do not do any code testing, there is no QA in place, they launch codes and simply destroy the plugin with each update, they release fixes, but brake other things. Bugs are not being fixed unless you report them on the community page and get enough votes, if there are not enough votes BUGs will simply stay in the code. They literally ask you to have paid support, just so you can report bugs and issues which will never get fixed. For 2 years I have seen close to no improvement, but rather degradation in the services even more. This reply was modified 7 years ago by TheSickle . Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 7 years ago Hello, We’d like to help you here but we can’t. We cannot provide any support for the PRO version here. Please contact us directly on our site. I am sure we will have no problem supporting you on our own site. Thread Starter vicegodgiarc (@vicegodgiarc) 7 years ago Hello Bookly, as I mentioned, this had nothing to do with PRO It had to do with the fact that 17.6 was broken and you just ignored our support requests and quietly rolled back to 17.5 without an appology or a note to say 17.6 is broken. I am all praise for good customer support and great products. Bookly is a GREAT product, but as others have said, your support is terrible and update releases are sometimes buggy. I’ll say it again BOOKLY IS A 5 Star product – the only issue is I HAVE to to a full end to end test to confirm everything is working when I update the plugins. Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 7 years ago Hello. We never release update only for free version, each Bookly item is connected to another and all Bookly items should be updated along with the core plugin. Which means that Bookly 17.6 won’t be working correctly with Pro 2.0, it requires the next version – Pro 2.1. If all your Bookly products are up to date and you still experience issues, please contact us directly on our site as we are not allowed to provide support here. Thread Starter vicegodgiarc (@vicegodgiarc) 7 years ago Possibly a hitch in the plugin services, because the additional plugins were not available at the release of 17.6? Search for: Search forums ALMOST awesome. geraldinedcarter (@geraldinedcarter) 11 years, 8 months ago Pretty easy to set up. I got a bit confused with Categories, Types, and Pricing, but was able to figure it out. Graphically, it’s nice and modern looking. Doesn’t look like dated Windows stuff (yuck). However, it got a low score on an at-home Usability test I did on my boyfriend. I asked him to try and schedule an appointment for himself, and he got really stuck with Step 1, entering his own availability. He was expecting to see a calendar of the provider’s availability first , and then narrow down his choices based on his availability after . I tried adding custom text to clarify what was going on and what the user should do, but he still got stuck. He’s not an uber-computer user, and some of my clients won’t be either. I want to see if going premium and adding Google Calendar integration fixes this, but I’m hard pressed to pay $38 to figure that out. I tried looking at the demos but didn’t gain insight. I REALLY want to like this plug-in; at the moment I’m a reluctant “ok, let me see if there’s anything better, and in the mean time I’ll use this and pray my clients don’t get to frustrated on page 1.” Happy to provide more insight to the developers – PM me if you like. Viewing 6 replies - 1 through 6 (of 6 total) Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 11 years, 8 months ago Hello. Thanks for your interest in Bookly and your feedback. We are trying to make Bookly flexible and easy-to-use for our customers. If you cinsider this feature confusing for your customers, you can hide the whole ‘I’m available on’ block, so it will disappear from the booking form. You can do this when adding the Booking form shortcode to the web page. In this case your customers can select the required service and go to the next page, where they can select convenient available slot to make reservation. Thanks Thread Starter geraldinedcarter (@geraldinedcarter) 11 years, 8 months ago Ok, great. Yes I would like to do this: “You can do this when adding the Booking form shortcode to the web page.” Can you be more specific? Do I go under Calendar, Appearance, Settings… or do I need to go into the .php somewhere, or edit the CSS? Thanks! Geraldine Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 11 years, 7 months ago Hi Geraldine, You need to open a page in the page edit mode. Then by pressing the Add Booking Form button above the text field, you can add the Booking form shortcode to the web page. By pressing this button you open a dialogue box, where you can define service category, services, and staff member that will be displayed on the booking form by default. In case you prefer to hide some of these fields from your clients, tick the Hide this field check box next to the required field. The field will disappear from the booking form. To hide the whole ‘I’m available on’ block, tick the Hide this field check box next to it. After that you need to click insert button and the booking form will appear on the web page. Thanks Plugin Author Bookly (@ladela) 11 years, 6 months ago Hi Geraldine, Hope you are doing well. Is Bookly working for you good? Can you please consider to revise your negative rating? Thanks MAX Website Design (@max-website-design) 11 years ago Hi Ladela, There is not an option to uncheck the “I’m Available on” block. Is there another way to remove this?
